static_traits.name: Zhao Danni
static_traits.educational_background: Master's degree in library and information science
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with colleagues affected by self-criticism; has a close friend, but has not yet shared feelings of incompetence as a librarian
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no treatment history for other psychological issues; never had similar issues before
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly, highly cooperative, slightly nervous but open; able to work with the counselor to set goals and plans

basic_info.main_problem: Believing oneself to be a 'bad librarian' for misshelving a book at work; since the incident, feelings of incompetence, overthinking and anxiety have emerged, affecting work and life.
basic_info.core_demands: Hoping to regain confidence at work and stop excessive anxiety and self-doubt.

special_situations.event: Put a book back on the wrong shelf in the library
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am making a mistake at work, it proves I am incompetent, a bad librarian
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Being extra careful, reinforcing organizing and checking procedures, repeatedly self-reviewing to avoid mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I shelved a book wrong, so I am a terrible librarian

special_situations.event: Worrying about poor organization when in charge of large book display tasks
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only being completely correct with zero errors shows I am competent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Continuously overthinks details during tasks and repeatedly double-checks, spending excessive time in pursuit of 'zero errors'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will surely mess up the display

special_situations.event: Facing multiple parallel library tasks, increased stress
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: When there are many tasks and high pressure, I will definitely lose control and make more mistakes
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying stricter organization and planning, over-preparation and checking beforehand
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Too many tasks and I will keep making mistakes, proving I am incompetent

special_situations.event: Every time an error occurs at work or a challenging situation is met
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Once feeling uneasy or doubtful, it means I am indeed incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Immediately engaging in self-criticism, constantly replaying details, hoping to avoid mistakes through self-blame
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I feel terrible, so I really am terrible

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized as professional and competent, and to maintain confidence and a sense of worth at work
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being seen as incompetent by colleagues or others, being criticized or negated, thus losing job satisfaction
defense_goal: Avoiding mistakes and external judgment through high self-monitoring and self-criticism
Stays cautious and avoids exposing vulnerability to gain a sense of safety

object_relations.self_representation: An incompetent employee who may make mistakes at any time
object_relations.object_representation: Picky colleagues who notice and judge mistakes

object_relations.self_representation: A person easily seen as exaggerating problems
object_relations.object_representation: Friends who may think I am 'overreacting'

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites more direct expression of vulnerable feelings and exploration of self-doubt sources
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Worrying that exposed vulnerability will be seen as 'overreacting' or not understood
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using a gentle, affirming tone; mostly using emotional reflection and body-feeling inquiries, guiding them to stay with emotional experience rather than only rational interpretation.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about whether to share feelings with close friends
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing expression will disturb others or be negated
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses a supportive tone to encourage small, tentative sharing, offering small steps and choices to lower her self-restraint.

manifestations: Living alone and not yet sharing feelings of work incompetence with close friends
Worries others think one is 'overreacting', and so keeps silent
outcomes: Relationship with colleagues affected, insufficient use of social support

manifestations: Declined work self-efficacy and satisfaction after the incident

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Overthinks and repeatedly checks every action at work
Persistent self-criticism, focusing attention on possible mistakes
Holding a cautious attitude toward plans in counseling, expressing 'still somewhat skeptical but willing to try'

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Not sharing one's own incompetence and anxiety with close friends
Presses the impulse to seek support outward back and turns it into self-blame and self-restraint

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Assuming friends will see oneself as 'overreacting', thus not expressing
Worries at work that colleagues are noticing and evaluating one's mistakes

positive_force: Willing to try and cooperate with the counselor (open and cooperative)
Possessing good organizational awareness and willingness to improve (proactively more careful, more structured)
In the past was always fairly confident at work, with a professional ability foundation
Has a close friend to confide in (a potential support resource)
negative_force: Tendencies of overgeneralization and catastrophizing, easily putting a global label on one mistake
Persistent overthinking and self-criticism; relies on external evaluation to define self-worth
High anticipated threat toward mistakes and challenging tasks, producing strong anxiety
Avoiding seeking support, leading to insufficient use of social support
Disrupted sleep and diet rhythms, further weakening emotion regulation

target_behavior.behavior: Persistent overthinking and self-doubt at work (worsened anxiety)
antecedent: Making mistakes at work (e.g. shelving a book wrongly)
When facing complex or important tasks (such as large displays)
Multiple tasks in parallel, increased stress
target_behavior.core_reason: Overgeneralizing one mistake into total incompetence, catastrophically predicting future failure, forming the rigid standard of 'must have zero errors to be competent'
target_behavior.function: Avoids the risk of criticism and making mistakes again, pursuing external recognition and a sense of safety
target_behavior.consequence: Increased work stress and exhaustion, affected performance, damaged relationships with colleagues, sleep and diet rhythm disturbance

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids expressing oneself to close friends and seeking support
antecedent: When thinking of sharing feelings, worries about being seen as 'overreacting'
When low mood or anxiety intensifies
target_behavior.core_reason: Excessive worry about others' evaluations and personalized interpretations, fearing self-exposure will bring negation
target_behavior.function: Avoiding potential shame and the risk of being negated
target_behavior.consequence: Increased sense of isolation, support system not yet utilized, negative emotions persisting
